ctx.x: get around, and that person wouldn't kill me until they got their fiddle, you know. It turned out later that it was Peck Morrison's bass. But however, naturally, we had to report it to the police, and that's when they started looking for me. That was before I went to Chicago, and I'm not thinking about that so much, because I knew he got his fiddle the next day; he got it back, but the police was still looking for me for petit petty larceny. And it didn't come to the floor until I got back there in '60, and I…

And, at that particular time, Frank Sinatra, as well as Sophie Tucker refused to work in New York in those big rooms unless they abolished that cabaret card business. And that made the police department mad, and they started going around raiding the clubs, and whoever had any kind of minor bust, you know, they were snatching their cards from them.

So naturally we had to look out for everything, so "I'll meet you in the morning, Jimmy says to me, we're gonna go down in the morning to get your cabaret card straightened out, you know, and reissue it to you because it had elapsed, and he said, "Yeah man, I got a Buell fiddle that you can have" -- and give me a bass.
